chapters.title: Chapter 6: From One Asset to Two — An Introduction to Pairs-Based Reversion

lessons.title: Where This Course Ends and Statistical Arbitrage Begins

children.text: This chapter was deliberately short. Three lessons are enough to show you why pairs-based reversion exists, why it can be more robust than betting on a single stock, and why correlation alone is not the property that makes it work. Three lessons are not enough to make you able to actually build and trade a pairs strategy safely, and pretending otherwise would do you a disservice. This closing lesson draws the line honestly: exactly what you now know, exactly what you don't yet, and exactly where to go for the rest.

body.text: This course goes deep on reversion in a single price, in volatility, and in valuation, the domains where the fullest, most complete treatment lives here. Multi-asset pairs trading and statistical arbitrage is a separate, complete discipline in its own right, built on formal cointegration testing and dynamic hedge ratios, and it deserves its own dedicated course rather than a rushed half-chapter here.

children.text: Why the Line Is Drawn Here

Single-asset, volatility, and valuation reversion, the subject of Chapters 2 through 5 and Chapters 7 and 8 ahead, is already a complete, self-contained discipline worth mastering fully on its own terms. Pairs trading and statistical arbitrage is a genuinely different skill set underneath the surface similarity, built on regression, formal hypothesis testing, and dynamic parameter estimation, that deserves the same depth this course gives everything else, not a compressed, partial version bolted onto the end of an already full syllabus. Everything you now know about market-neutrality, idiosyncratic risk, and the correlation-cointegration distinction is not wasted effort if you go no further. It is also not wasted if you eventually do, since it is exactly the conceptual foundation Introduction to Statistical Arbitrage builds its own first chapters on top of.
What Comes Next, in This Course

From here, this course returns to the single-asset toolkit built in Chapters 2 through 5. Chapter 7 turns z-score, half-life, Bollinger Bands, RSI, and moving-average reversion into a complete, disciplined trading system: precise entry and exit rules, position sizing and stop-losses, a full Python backtest on a multi-signal strategy, and the common backtesting traps, look-ahead bias, overfitting, and survivorship bias, that quietly inflate a strategy's apparent performance. Chapter 8 closes the course with the hardest and most important question running through everything so far: how do you recognize, in real time and not just in hindsight, the moment a reversion strategy stops working because the regime underneath it has genuinely changed.

body.text: If you do go on to study statistical arbitrage properly, you will already recognize market-neutrality, idiosyncratic versus systematic risk, and why correlation is not cointegration the moment they reappear. That head start is this chapter's real purpose, not a substitute for the fuller treatment itself.

body.explanation: Chapter 6 deliberately covers only the conceptual groundwork: why a two-asset relationship can be more robust than a single-asset bet, and why correlation alone does not establish a tradeable relationship. The formal testing, hedge ratio construction, and full strategy-building machinery are explicitly out of scope here and are covered in Introduction to Statistical Arbitrage.

points: This chapter covered why pairs-based reversion can be more robust than single-asset reversion, and why correlation alone does not establish that a pair is genuinely tradeable, without covering the formal testing or strategy-building mechanics.

Formal cointegration testing, dynamic hedge ratios, entry and exit rules for a spread, and factor-based statistical arbitrage are covered in full in the companion course, Introduction to Statistical Arbitrage.

The line is drawn here deliberately: single-asset, volatility, and valuation reversion is a complete discipline this course covers fully, and pairs trading is a genuinely separate discipline that deserves its own equally complete treatment.
Everything learned in this chapter, market-neutrality, idiosyncratic risk, correlation versus cointegration, directly carries over as a head start if you go on to study statistical arbitrage.
Chapter 7 now returns to the single-asset toolkit from Chapters 2 to 5 and turns it into a complete, disciplined trading system.

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and is not investment advice or a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any security. References to Introduction to Statistical Arbitrage describe that course's own scope and content, which may be updated over time. Pairs trading and statistical arbitrage strategies carry real risk of loss and require formal statistical testing and regulatory compliance before being deployed with real capital. Consult a SEBI-registered investment adviser or research analyst before trading.
